subject: social-studies
title: The Globalisation Supply Chain of One Smartphone

segments.say: Mine raw materials: value rises to $10 of value. Lithium and metals are dug out of the ground in Country A, and the value bar rises to $10 - the least the phone will ever be worth. Point at the route arrow leaving the scene on your student notes before it lands in the next country.
questions: What is mined in this scene, and what value does the bar reach?
Where does the route arrow carry the materials?

segments.say: Make the components: value rises to $35 of value. Factories in Country B turn the raw materials into chips, screens and batteries, and making parts lifts the value to $35. Now try the components-country questions on your worksheet.
questions: What do the factories in Country B gain from the materials mined in Country A?
In which country are the components made?

segments.say: Assemble the phone: value rises to $70 of value. The components travel on to Country C, where they are assembled into one finished smartphone; the value bar rises from $35 to $70 because a working phone is worth more than loose parts. Check the order of the stages against your student notes before moving on.
questions: Why does assembly add more value than the components alone?
What does the value bar rise from, and to, in this scene?

segments.say: Sell it in Singapore: value rises to $120 of value. The finished phone is shipped to a shop shelf in Singapore, where transport, branding and retail bring the value to $120. Keep the whole chain - Country A $10, Country B $35, Country C $70, Singapore $120 - in view as you check your student notes and finish the exit ticket.
questions: What exactly happens to the phone in Singapore?
What is the whole supply chain, in order?
segments.watchFor: A global product is made entirely in the country where it is sold, because every stage of making it happens in one place. Listen for students who treat the phone as made in the shop's country because it carries one brand. Send them back to the route arrows: A global product crosses borders at every stage: raw materials are mined in one country, components are made in a second, the product is assembled in a third, and only then is it shipped to the shop shelf in Singapore - value is added at every handover along the chain.
